name: Stuxnet
summary: First known cyber weapon to cause physical damage, degrading roughly a thousand uranium-enrichment centrifuges at Natanz.

name: Sony Pictures breach
summary: Destructive intrusion and mass data leak attributed by the FBI to North Korea; wiped systems and exposed employee data and unreleased films.

name: Anthem breach
summary: Health insurer breach exposing personal data of 78.8 million people; settled with US regulators.

name: OPM breach
summary: US Office of Personnel Management breach exposing security-clearance records of 21.5 million people, including fingerprints.

name: Ukraine power grid (2015)
summary: First confirmed cyberattack to take down an electricity grid, cutting power to about 230,000 people in western Ukraine.

name: Bangladesh Bank heist
summary: Fraudulent SWIFT transfers stole US$81 million from Bangladesh Bank's account at the New York Fed; attributed to the Lazarus Group.

name: Ukraine grid / Industroyer (2016)
summary: Purpose-built grid malware (Industroyer/CrashOverride) cut power in Kyiv; the first malware designed specifically to attack electricity infrastructure.

name: WannaCry
summary: Self-propagating ransomworm hit ~200,000 computers across 150 countries; forced cancellation of thousands of NHS appointments. Global cost estimates run into the billions.

name: NotPetya
summary: Destructive wiper disguised as ransomware, spread via a Ukrainian tax-software update; the most financially damaging cyberattack on record, with global losses estimated around US$10 billion.

name: Equifax breach
summary: Credit bureau breach exposing personal and financial data of ~147 million people; led to a settlement of up to US$700 million.

name: Marriott / Starwood breach
summary: Long-running intrusion in the Starwood reservation system exposed up to ~339 million guest records; fined £18.4m by the UK ICO.

name: Capital One breach
summary: Misconfigured cloud storage exposed ~106 million credit-card applicants; US$80m regulatory penalty plus a US$190m settlement.

name: Baltimore ransomware
summary: RobbinHood ransomware disrupted City of Baltimore services for weeks; recovery and lost revenue estimated at over US$18 million.

name: SolarWinds / SUNBURST
summary: Compromised SolarWinds Orion updates reached ~18,000 organisations and were used to breach nine US federal agencies; a landmark software supply-chain espionage campaign.

name: Colonial Pipeline
summary: DarkSide ransomware forced the shutdown of the largest US fuel pipeline, triggering regional shortages; US$4.4m ransom paid, much later recovered.

name: HSE Ireland ransomware
summary: Conti ransomware crippled Ireland's national health service IT for weeks; the independent review put the cost at over €80 million.

name: Kaseya VSA supply-chain
summary: REvil exploited Kaseya's remote-management software to push ransomware to ~1,500 downstream businesses in one weekend; a US$70m universal ransom was demanded.

name: Viasat KA-SAT wiper
summary: AcidRain wiper knocked out Viasat KA-SAT modems at the start of the invasion of Ukraine, with spillover disabling remote monitoring of thousands of European wind turbines.

name: Costa Rica / Conti
summary: Conti ransomware paralysed Costa Rican government systems and tax and customs services; the president declared a national emergency - a first for a cyberattack.

name: Medibank breach
summary: Breach of Australia's largest health insurer exposed data of 9.7 million current and former customers, including sensitive health claims.

name: MOVEit / Cl0p
summary: Cl0p exploited a zero-day in MOVEit Transfer to steal data from thousands of organisations, with tens of millions of individuals affected downstream.

name: 23andMe credential-stuffing
summary: Credential-stuffing exposed genetic and profile data of ~6.9 million people via the DNA-testing service.

name: Change Healthcare
summary: ALPHV/BlackCat ransomware crippled the largest US medical-claims clearinghouse, disrupting payments nationwide for months; ~190 million people affected, the largest US healthcare breach on record. Parent company costs ran into the billions.
